global.pefExplainer: Le PEF (Product Environmental Footprint) évalue l'empreinte environnementale globale d'un processus (utilisation de ressources, impacts sur la santé humaine, destruction d'écosystèmes), alors que les seuils mensuels planétaires par habitant évaluent la stabilité du système Terre et sa pérennité.

heatmap.title: Monthly threshold per inhabitant hotspot map (nodes × indicators)

interpretation.bothAbove: This criterion exceeds two benchmarks at once: 25% of the sustainable monthly budget per person and 1 mPt of PEF score. It therefore weighs both on planetary boundaries and on the overall environmental balance. The PEF score aggregates impacts on human health, ecosystems and resources into a single score: here, the area at stake is {area}.
interpretation.ratioAbove: This criterion exceeds 25% of the sustainable monthly budget per person: it therefore weighs on planetary boundaries. Its contribution to the PEF score remains low, however, so its weight in the overall environmental balance (human health, ecosystems, resources) stays limited.
interpretation.pefAbove: This criterion stays below 25% of the sustainable monthly budget per person, but its contribution to the PEF score exceeds 1 mPt: it therefore weighs on the overall environmental balance, even though its pressure on planetary boundaries remains low. The PEF score aggregates impacts on human health, ecosystems and resources into a single score: here, the area at stake is {area}.
interpretation.bothBelow: This criterion stays below both benchmarks: 25% of the sustainable monthly budget per person and 1 mPt of PEF score. Its pressure on planetary boundaries and its weight in the overall environmental balance (human health, ecosystems, resources) therefore remain low.

PEF-GWP.label: Climate change
PEF-GWP.description: Global warming potential (GWP), the most common indicator of carbon footprint.

PEF-ODP.label: Ozone depletion
PEF-ODP.description: Destruction of the stratospheric ozone layer.

PEF-PM.label: Fine particulates
PEF-PM.description: Fine particulate emissions and their impact on human health.

PEF-AP.label: Acidification
PEF-AP.description: Acidification of soils and water (acid rain).

PEF-IR.label: Ionizing radiation
PEF-IR.description: Impact on human health from ionizing radiation.

PEF-POCP.label: Photochemical ozone
PEF-POCP.description: Tropospheric ozone formation (smog) affecting human health.

PEF-CTUh-nc.label: Human toxicity (non-carc.)
PEF-CTUh-nc.description: Non-carcinogenic toxic effects on human health.

PEF-ADPf.label: Fossil depletion
PEF-ADPf.description: Depletion of fossil abiotic resources (primary energy).

PEF-ADPe.label: Mineral/metal depletion
PEF-ADPe.description: Depletion of mineral and metal resources.

PEF-WU.label: Water use
PEF-WU.description: Freshwater consumption. The LCA (PEF-WU, in m³ eq) and the ecologits contribution (WCF, in litres) are not merged because they come from different methodologies: they are shown side by side as two distinct contributions.

PEF-CTUh-c.label: Human toxicity (carc.)
PEF-CTUh-c.description: Carcinogenic toxic effects on human health.
